results.reason: Issue 1 states the renewal deadline (~Aug. 16, 2026) has passed with no notice shown. It says the agreement expires Nov. 14, 2026, before the Nov. 30 closing. It flags MIPA § 3.12(c) and Schedule 3.12 as inaccurate, with indemnity and fraud exposure for the Sellers.

Issue 2 identifies the 100% sale as a Change of Control requiring prior written consent under § 14.2, with an immediate termination right. It notes the consent is omitted from Schedule 3.6 and so falls outside § 6.4 and § 7.1(d). It recommends obtaining consent before Closing and adding it to Schedule 3.6.

Issue 6 says the Side Letter redefines Territory to add NY and VA and that the Side Letter ranks above the agreement under § 19.4. It says the non-compete burden extends to six states while exclusivity covers four, and recommends conforming the territories. The response calls the precedence point ambiguous, but the substance is there.

Issue 6 identifies the Side Letter's New York law and New York County forum against the Delaware law and Wilmington forum in §§ 18.1–18.2. It explains that disputes could be split between two courts and two bodies of law, and recommends aligning law and forum with Delaware.
The response states the Initial Term ends Nov. 14, 2026.
The response states the target Closing is Nov. 30, 2026 (MIPA § 2.2).
The response states the Distribution Agreement Territory is DE, MD, NJ and PA only (§ 1.12).
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner. Each issue has Where, Issue, Why it matters and Recommendation sections.
Issues are ordered most significant first, labeled CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM and LOWER. Part 4 flags the items to raise promptly with the client and with Quillon's counsel.
The response states there is no auto-renewal and that 'a notice delivered now would be late.' It treats a protective notice only as a weak fallback.
The response expressly states that Schedule 3.6 omits Velloran and that the § 6.4 covenant and § 7.1(d) condition do not reach it.
